summary: Replay classes, the selected-run Safe rerun, and parent-SIGKILL checkpoint tests at 519a202b13, the develop commit that squashes slice C and the commit every HEAD run tested. The Linux preflight passed 33 gates (actionlint and the TypeScript runtime gate skipped) on its second attempt, under umask 022; the first, under umask 077, failed scripts-unit and rust-package because the unpacked bake-rs had mode 0700. The Intel x86_64 macOS native preflight passed its 4 gates, and both rust gates ran every test this slice added. Every tool bake-rs composes, MCP included, carries a replay class, and flipping or clearing the class and read_only on every tool leaves the request transcript and three provider bodies byte-identical. bake-rs -p --session <file> --resume-run <id> reaches AgentSession::resume_run (print_mode.rs), which now reruns interrupted calls only when every unresolved call is on the run's last assistant, each tool is Safe now and, if dispatched, was recorded Safe, and the run is otherwise resumable; ordinary recovery still sends No result provided and runs nothing. On Linux and Intel macOS the tests SIGKILL a fixture child 20 times per run and check its file, the next request, and an effect count shared by both processes. Seven checkpoint mutations, each run once on an uncommitted tree before the slice's final amend, were each rejected. This is the first scope 08 record. Windows runs, power loss, kills inside write or during streamed bytes, a CLI test of a crashed run's Safe rerun, logs of the worker's repeat run and rerun mutations, an eval record, and Auto review remain. Before push the stack was rebased onto develop c5f02c476a (scope 12 web tools and hooks, scope 15 commands), which changed every hash: this record's candidate 519a202b13 became d8c2e3c691 and its base 72b43cd2cc became 8fdc5e13b1, with the fixture bytes unchanged. The runs above at 519a202b13 are pre-rebase. A second run set at bfdbbcb875, the rebased stack with three integration commits on top (Windows lint fixes in the scope 12 and 15 code, D41's inconclusive loopback timeout, and Never replay classes for web_search and web_fetch), passed: the Linux preflight's 33 gates (actionlint and the TypeScript runtime skipped; 2534 Cargo tests, 6 ignored; PTY 58/58), the Intel macOS native preflight's 4 gates (2512, 6 ignored; PTY 56/56), and cross-target Clippy for Windows and Apple Silicon. A dispatched CI run of the scratch branch ci/qualify-win-mac (https://github.com/Justar96/bake/actions/runs/39206590298) then ran the whole workspace with --no-fail-fast at 9111a94546, which is develop's later fix commit 54e9a05872 plus one commit changing only .github/workflows/ci.yml: windows-latest passed 2397 tests with 7 ignored, and macos-latest (Apple Silicon) 2554 with 6 ignored; that commit's own fixes are named in its history. The same run's native preflight failed only Windows rust-pty, on five inline ConPTY scenarios that failed on every earlier Windows run too.

oracle.notApplicable: D32: no TypeScript runtime arm. Pi v1.3.0 (71023aec15) gives its built-in tools no replay class; the rerun rule follows Pi Durable's harness/tool.ts, which reruns an interrupted execute phase only when the stored and the current class are both safe and records an absent class as unsafe. Bake departs from it as D37 requires: a rerun goes through the current hooks, plugin vetoes, journal dispatch, and permission wrappers, and a call that is not Safe leaves the run needing reconciliation instead of settling it with an interruption error. Pi's source was read, not run.

results.behavior: every_composed_tool_has_a_replay_class_no_request_carries passed on Linux and Intel macOS. It builds the session through cli::start_interactive with --model faux/faux-1 --permission danger-full-access --no-session --tools *, a home whose settings enable task documents, schedules, and subagents, two faux models, and a real stdio MCP fixture server from the home's mcp.json, then sends one prompt. The tools the agent executes have no tool without a class and match exactly REPLAY_CLASSES (19 built-ins: read, grep, find, ls, job_list, schedule_list, list_subagent_models, and list_agents Safe; bash, edit, write, job_output, job_kill, subagent, send_message, interrupt_agent, task_document, schedule_create, and schedule_delete Never) plus the nine MCP fixture tools as Never, with no name repeated. The session's own request declares exactly each tool's declaration(). Flipping every class (Safe to Never, anything else to Safe) and negating read_only, or clearing both, leaves the transcript and the OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages bodies byte-identical. Counts describe Cargo tests.

subagents::tests::every_subagent_tool_has_a_replay_class passed on Linux and Intel macOS: the parent's subagent, list_subagent_models, send_message, interrupt_agent, and list_agents are Never, Safe, Never, Never, and Safe, and the child's send_message, which a parent never composes, is Never.

The seven run_journal_tests::rerun:: tests passed on Linux and Intel macOS; each writes a real session file at the interruption and counts each tool's executions. safe_calls_rerun_under_the_current_policy_before_the_notice: a call dispatched Safe and one never dispatched are Resumable; resume_run runs each once, makes one request (user, assistant, both results, then the recovery notice), writes each dispatch with safe, its result, and its ack before the recovery entry, and leaves the run Completed with 2 model calls. a_rerun_the_current_policy_denies_is_not_run: a current plugin veto answers the rerun with its error result before the notice and the tool runs 0 times; a tool now inactive, Never, or unclassified leaves the run NeedsReconciliation, resume_run fails with external effect, no request is made, and no resumed record is written. a_call_that_is_not_safe_needs_reconciliation_and_never_repeats covers seven cases, including a dispatch with no class or recorded never, a Safe call beside a pending Never call, a spent budget, and a later user turn: no request, no tool run. completed_calls_on_the_same_assistant_do_not_block_a_rerun, only_a_later_resumption_dispatches_a_safe_call_again (a repeat Safe dispatch is valid only after a Resumed record), and a_dispatch_records_only_a_safe_class_and_reads_no_other (a recorded class of unsafe, SAFE, true, or null makes the journal invalid) also passed.

rerun::ordinary_recovery_answers_no_result_provided_and_reruns_nothing passed on Linux and Intel macOS: an ordinary prompt after the same interruption runs no tool, and its request, passed through the providers' transform_messages, carries result first (error): No result provided before the new user turn. The plain-assistant case of kill::a_kill_after_a_synced_tool_call_and_before_its_effect_runs_nothing shows the same after a real SIGKILL, with an effect count of 0.

On Linux and Intel macOS the four run_journal_tests::kill:: tests, process_crashes_preserve_recovery_boundaries_without_replaying_effects, and jobs::crash_after_job_wait_start_refuses_a_refunded_deadline_and_never_replays_the_job passed. kill_fixture re-runs the test binary as a child, waits up to 60 s for its ready marker (the child parks a thread at the kill point), kills it, and on unix asserts the status's signal is SIGKILL; a run kills 20 children (13 kill points in the kill tests, 6 in process_crashes, and the job-wait child). After each kill the test reopens the file in this process and checks its entries, the next request, and an effect count kept as synced lines in the test's own directory. A new session killed at its first request holds system and user, is listed with that prompt, and the next prompt sends both user turns. A recoverable run killed before a call's dispatch record or after it and before the effect needs reconciliation, makes no request, runs no effect, and leaves the file unchanged; a Safe probe killed there or after its effect reruns once with the notice; an effect killed after it ran is counted once and never repeated. Kills at the request after a retry, a queued follow-up, a steer queued from inside a running tool, a threshold compaction, and a job notice find each input on disk before its request and resume carrying it. Each request kill parks inside the faux provider call before any byte streams. An earlier run of mutate-kill.py (mutate-kill.out, last written at 00:38:38), before the job-notice case and under the old test name a_kill_at_a_retried_followed_up_steered_or_compacted_request_keeps_its_input, applied the six mutations other than notice-unacked to a filter that ran 4 tests (884 filtered out); each failed at least one.

AgentSession::resume_run, which holds the Safe rerun, is reached from the command line: in rust/crates/bake-coding-agent/src/print_mode.rs (lines 214-221 at 519a202b13), PrintRunRecovery::Resume, selected by bake-rs -p --session <file> --resume-run <id>, refuses any new prompt, piped input, or file and calls session.resume_run.
